themes_detail.label: Graffiti explosion in Flatbush
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints spiked to 102 THIS WEEK—a 1940% increase from the 8-week average of 5.0 per week—suggesting a sudden, coordinated outbreak or gang activity that requires immediate investigation and cleanup coordination.
evidence: 102 graffiti complaints THIS WEEK vs. 5.0 per week baseline (1940% spike, z-score: 14.38)
Highest z-score among all 311 spikes, indicating most statistically anomalous event in district
Pattern suggests concentrated incident rather than gradual deterioration
reporting_angles: Map where graffiti complaints cluster geographically—are specific blocks or corridors targeted?
Interview NYPD, Sanitation, and Parks on response coordination and cleanup timeline

themes_detail.label: Vehicle noise surge
themes_detail.summary: Vehicle noise complaints jumped to 23 THIS WEEK—a 426% increase from the 8-week average of 4.4 per week—indicating possible illegal street racing, motorcycle activity, or construction vehicle congestion that warrants monitoring.
evidence: 23 vehicle noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 4.4 per week average (426% spike, z-score: 11.26)
Complements broader noise trend: residential noise (1506 total complaints) + street/sidewalk noise spike (63 complaints last week, 282% above baseline)
Non-emergency police matters also up 261% last week (14 vs. 3.9 avg), suggesting public safety concern
reporting_angles: Canvass residents on specific times and locations—is this late-night street racing or daytime delivery/construction noise?
Interview NYPD on enforcement of noise ordinances and vehicle modification laws

themes_detail.label: Park rule violations uptick
themes_detail.summary: Park rule violation complaints reached 4 THIS WEEK—a 967% spike from the 8-week average of 0.4 per week—suggesting new enforcement activity, overcrowding, or unmanaged use issues at Prospect Park or Parade Grounds.
evidence: 4 park rule violation complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 per week baseline (967% spike, z-score: 7.49)
Community board has standing request to 'improve access to park or amenity,' suggesting ongoing park quality concerns
Could reflect response to broader park safety or overcrowding issues
reporting_angles: Identify which parks are affected and what specific violations are being reported (dogs off-leash, after-hours use, unsafe activities)
Interview Parks Dept. and CB on whether this reflects new enforcement or actual behavior change

themes_detail.label: Street/sidewalk noise wave
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints reached 63 LAST WEEK—a 282% increase from the 8-week average of 16.5 per week—indicating sustained disruption from street vendors, music, construction, or pedestrian congestion affecting quality of life.
evidence: 63 street/sidewalk noise complaints LAST WEEK vs. 16.5 per week average (282% spike, z-score: 4.99)
Part of broader noise crisis: residential noise at 1506 total complaints (3rd highest category over 90 days)
Overlaps with vehicle noise spike, suggesting multi-source noise problem affecting sleep and quality of life
reporting_angles: Identify noise sources by location and time of day—street fairs, late-night bars, delivery trucks, construction?
Profile a block or corridor experiencing peak complaints; interview residents on impact to daily life

themes_detail.label: Dead animal complaint cluster
themes_detail.summary: Dead animal complaints reached 6 LAST WEEK—a 269% increase from the 8-week average of 1.6 per week—potentially signaling pest infestation, environmental contamination, or inadequate Sanitation response that warrants health inquiry.
evidence: 6 dead animal complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.6 per week baseline (269% spike, z-score: 5.11)
Residential disposal complaints also up 126% last week (13 vs. 5.8 avg), suggesting broader sanitation/waste issue
Could indicate rodent or raccoon problem tied to unsanitary conditions (725 complaints over 90 days, 6th highest category)
reporting_angles: Verify if complaints cluster geographically—does one block or area have disproportionate dead animals?
Interview NYC Sanitation on response times and whether this correlates with recent pest control operations
